title: Persist XKBLAYOUT for LUKS so non-US layouts stay typeable
head: c37fb5eb4f7c
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A failed first UKI rebuild is never retried after the migration successfully writes XKBLAYOUT
leads.consequence: If sudo limine-mkinitcpio fails after XKBLAYOUT is appended, the migration exits nonzero without a marker. On the next login the config already has XKBLAYOUT, the changed flag is 0 and line 26 exits successfully without attempting the build. omarchy-migrate then creates its marker at :95, leaving the old UKI in place (and the LUKS prompt unchanged) until an unrelated rebuild. Rebuild failure or cancelled sudo after the first successful write suffices. Keep a durable pending-rebuild signal or retry when the previous rebuild did not complete.

leads.summary: KEYMAP=cz is converted to the wrong XKB variant and can newly break a working Czech boot passphrase
leads.consequence: The offered Czech choice is console KEYMAP=cz. There is no cz row in systemd 261's kbd-model-map, so the two-letter fallback writes XKBLAYOUT=cz without XKBVARIANT=qwerty, and the hook bundles it. kbd's cz console is QWERTY (keycodes 21/44 y/z), while XKB cz's default is QWERTZ (AD06/AB01 z/y). On Arch Plymouth 26.134.222-3 the KEYMAP-only state used the legacy VT input (Arch cherry-picks the keymap fallback fix), so this PR can switch an existing, working boot prompt to the wrong y/z positions. A passphrase containing y or z typed at enrollment fails on the next boot. Use a verified cz/qwerty mapping. The premise that KEYMAP-only necessarily falls back to US contradicts the shipped patched Plymouth when KEYMAP is present; this matters when assessing the benefit of other forced XKB writes, too.

leads.summary: The Serbian hook fix does not reach existing UKIs whose rs/latin settings were already complete
leads.consequence: systemd 261 already maps sr-latin to XKBLAYOUT=rs XKBVARIANT=latin. An install with that config previously built a UKI with no vconsole.conf because the old hook excluded rs. The new hook would include rs/latin, but the migration skips rebuilding because the helper writes nothing. Updating omarchy-settings alone does not match limine-mkinitcpio-hook 1.39.0's pacman rebuild trigger paths. Thus the old UKI remains until a separate kernel/initramfs rebuild; a Serbian Latin passphrase differing from US key placement stays mistyped. Trigger one build for already-complete Latin variants newly admitted by the hook, or explicitly arrange a rebuild on hook upgrade.

leads.summary: Three offered console choices remain without any XKB mapping: azerty, bg-cp1251, kyrgyz
leads.consequence: systemd 261 has no rows for these three offered names, and none match the new hardcoded or two-letter fallbacks; the helper returns without changing KEYMAP-only vconsole.conf. On a stock desktop default/hypr/input.lua uses us, so the Azerbaijani-labelled azerty choice (actually a French AZERTY console map) cannot type the same Latin password on the desktop, and Bulgarian/Kyrgyz users do not receive their chosen desktop script. The latter should remain excluded from Latin LUKS boot configuration, but still need verified desktop XKB mappings; the console azerty should map to the correct Latin variant rather than stay US. This is remaining picker coverage, not a claim that the new commits introduced those existing omissions.
leads.triage: dropped; pre-existing picker gap, not caused by PR

leads.summary: The protected-file sudo sed branch replaces administrator vconsole.conf symlinks
leads.consequence: When a protected /etc/vconsole.conf is a symlink to a managed file and already has XKBLAYOUT= empty, sudo sed -i replaces the symlink itself by a regular file. The original managed target retains its old layout. A later configuration re-link silently reverts the persisted boot layout; package/admin overrides lose their link. Use sed -i --follow-symlinks (or update the resolved target safely) when replacement is intended.
leads.triage: dropped; symlink edge; unprivileged sed -i behaves the same

leads.summary: A later administrator XKB override is overwritten when an earlier blank assignment is present
leads.consequence: The helper's awk reads only the first XKBLAYOUT= and reports it empty. For KEYMAP=fr followed by XKBLAYOUT= then a later XKBLAYOUT=ru override, it replaces *both* matching lines via sed -i, even though the Lua desktop consumer and shell-sourced hook used the last, ru, value before migration. The desktop now silently switches to fr, contrary to the ordinary-admin-override guarantee. Detect the effective value with the same semantics as each consumer, and replace only the intended entry or preserve a later explicit override. Plymouth's groupless key-file has its own duplicate semantics, so avoid asserting that it used the later value.
leads.triage: dropped; duplicate-key admin edge, low value

leads.summary: Open PRs #11418 and #9358 both conflict with this PR's keyboard integration
leads.consequence: Both other heads are diverged, not stacked. A three-way text merge from each actual common ancestor produces conflict markers: #11418 in input.lua and apply_keyboard, #9358 in apply_keyboard. Accepting #11418's keyboard.lua without reconciling this PR loses the rs/latin desktop exemption; choosing this PR's side of #9358's owner conflict drops its XKB-only Thai branch. Integrate both behaviors explicitly. GitHub marks #11418 and #9358 MERGEABLE relative to each's own base, not compatible with this head.
leads.triage: partially_used; #11418 overlap already in Opus N1; merge conflict detail not verified, not published

leads.summary: New protected-file test never covers the privileged replacement path
leads.consequence: Its protected fixture contains KEYMAP=fr but no XKBLAYOUT. The setter therefore invokes sudo tee -a, not sudo sed -i. A plausible regression with a missing/incorrect sudo on the sed -i branch still passes this entire test, while existing protected configurations with XKBLAYOUT= empty fail at the migration. Add a protected existing XKBLAYOUT= case asserting the sudo sed invocation and resulting value. The current test's sudo stub also flips permissions to mimic elevation rather than testing real sudo (intentional fixture limitation).

leads.summary: Root-side configuration reference omits the new keyboard setup step
leads.consequence: The root-side install overview lists the steps sourced by install/config/all.sh, but still lacks the newly inserted keyboard-vconsole step. Readers using the reference to trace when vconsole.conf is written and when UKI is built do not see the new write. Add it to the config/all.sh step list at line 311.
leads.triage: dropped; docs summary list, low value

limits: The Arch Plymouth package is pinned to 26.134.222-3 by its packaging source dated 2026-09-24; the cherry-pick patch was read but a full machine boot with a particular passphrase was not attempted. The Czech y/z consequence follows the shipped input sources, not a booted machine.
#11418's merge conflicts preclude a meaningful merged test before a human chooses how to resolve both sections; no claim that #11418 itself is unmergeable against its own base.

Additional open PR search returned many unrelated hardware/lock PRs from broad topic words. Overlapping keyboard PRs are recorded in inventory.json; no guarantee that all concurrently opened PRs were inspected.

prior_findings.claim: Migration calls omarchy_ensure_vconsole_xkb unprivileged; write to protected /etc/vconsole.conf fails, migration exits 1, later migrations stop.
prior_findings.reason: Setter elevates with sudo sed -i / sudo tee -a when not writable; old head reproduced exit 1 under same model; head exit 0 with one rebuild; sudo failure exits 1 before rebuild. Author claim confirmed.

prior_findings.claim: sr-latin: hook excludes rs without considering Latin variant.
prior_findings.reason: Drop-in bundles rs with latin* variant; migration and Hyprland treat rs/latin as Latin.

prior_findings.claim: no-latin1 and de_CH-latin1 KEYMAP-only configurations do not gain the intended Latin-layout path into Plymouth.
prior_findings.reason: Factual part (no map row, helper wrote nothing) was right; impact was wrong: base drop-in bundles KEYMAP-only file, keymap hook loads console keymap, and Arch Plymouth 24.004.60-x and 26.134.222-2+ read keys through the VT keymap when XKBLAYOUT is unset. Only 26.134.222-1 (one week) defaulted to US XKB.

Helper writes XKB layouts (cz, no, ch(de_nodeadkeys)) that differ from the enrolled console keymap on plain/Shift keys; migration rebuilds, moving existing users' LUKS prompt off the console keymap. Corroborated by Sol H01 (cz).
Arch plymouth 26.134.222-3 hook bundles non-empty vconsole.conf, bypassing Omarchy's exclusion; PR fallback writes XKBLAYOUT=ua giving Cyrillic XKB prompt.
Migration rebuild decision keyed on per-run CHANGED flag; failed rebuild then retry marks migration complete with no rebuild. Sol lead H09, confirmed by Opus follow-up run.
Drop-in ${XKBVARIANT%%,*} not set -u safe; test prints unbound variable. Published as Optional note.

# Retrospective: t3-12896-58b837fc

## What worked
- The Sol hunter found the retry-state gap (H09) that Opus had not reported; a neutral follow-up let Opus confirm it with the real migration runner.
- The Opus self-check caught 9 flags, including two over-claims that came from its own report (colemak/pl "every key", "reproduce the console keymap"). All were fixed before editorial.
- The follow-up corrected an earlier public impact claim (F2b) from dependency source rather than defending it.

## Friction
- `release` moved `opus/src/wt-head`, whose Git alternates used absolute paths, so the checkout broke. Opus made a fresh `src/wt-head-2` for the follow-up. Suggest creating reviewer worktrees without absolute alternates, or noting that release breaks them.
- The first editorial check flagged a **Minor:** label as a severity prefix. Drafts should use **Optional (...)** for small notes.
- I initially mis-stated one cell in the ua table ("not bundled" without the PR). I caught it before the self-check. Keymap-only files are bundled by the base drop-in.

## Carry forward
- For keyboard/initramfs PRs, check the Arch packaging hook as well as Omarchy's drop-in; packaging changes can bypass Omarchy's FILES logic.
comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12896#issuecomment-5778906719) of `e97fe6d2`, checked at `c37fb5eb`, after the author's [reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12896#issuecomment-5841738739).

| Earlier finding | Outcome at `c37fb5eb` |
| --- | --- |
| Migration config write was unprivileged | **Resolved** |
| Serbian `sr-latin` excluded from the initramfs | **Resolved**, for the next initramfs rebuild |
| Norwegian `no-latin1` and Swiss German `de_CH-latin1` lacked a Plymouth path | **Withdrawn**: the earlier impact claim was wrong (see below) |

Three new issues follow: the new XKB mappings differ from the enrolled console keymap for some layouts, `XKBLAYOUT=ua` becomes a risk with Arch's newest Plymouth package, and a failed rebuild is not retried.

**Verified:** `omarchy_vconsole_set` now uses `sudo sed -i` or `sudo tee -a` when the config is not writable. The migration runner uses `bash -euo pipefail`, so a failed elevation stops the migration before any rebuild.

| Protected config, `KEYMAP=fr` | `e97fe6d2` | `c37fb5eb` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sudo succeeds | exit 1, `Permission denied` | exit 0, `XKBLAYOUT=fr` written, one rebuild |
| sudo fails | exit 1 | exit 1, config unchanged, no rebuild |
| `XKBLAYOUT` already set | exit 0 | exit 0, no sudo call, no rebuild |

**Verified:** the drop-in now bundles `XKBLAYOUT=rs` with a `latin*` variant, while `rs` without a variant, `ru,us` and `ua` stay excluded. `omarchy_layout_is_non_latin rs latin` returns Latin, and Hyprland no longer prepends `us` for `rs/latin`. systemd-firstboot already writes `rs/latin` for `sr-latin`, so on existing installs the migration writes nothing and does not rebuild. The new drop-in applies at the next initramfs rebuild, for example after a kernel update.

**Correction (`no-latin1`, `de_CH-latin1`):** the earlier review said these KEYMAP-only configurations did not gain the intended Latin-layout path into Plymouth. That was wrong for the Plymouth builds Arch ships:
- The base drop-in already bundles a KEYMAP-only `vconsole.conf`.
- mkinitcpio's `keymap` hook loads that console keymap before `encrypt` asks for the passphrase.
- With `KEYMAP` set and no `XKBLAYOUT`, Plymouth reads keys from the VT through that keymap. This holds for Arch's 24.004.60 builds and for 26.134.222-2 and later, which cherry-pick upstream `cea90be`. Only 26.134.222-1, current for about a week in May 2026, fell back to US XKB.

The missing map rows were real, but the passphrase prompt already used the same console keymap the passphrase was enrolled under.

### New XKB mappings differ from the enrolled console keymap

For KEYMAP-only files, the helper now writes an XKB layout whenever it finds a mapping. Once `XKBLAYOUT` is set, Plymouth uses the XKB layout instead of the console keymap the passphrase was typed under. Of the 48 layouts in the setup form, the helper changes six: `colemak`, `cz`, `de_CH-latin1`, `no-latin1`, `pl` and `ua`. `colemak` and `pl` matched on the plain and Shift levels of every key compared, though some AltGr positions differ. Three differ on plain or Shift keys (key tables from kbd 2.10.0 `loadkeys --mktable` against `xkbcli compile-keymap` with the test host's xkeyboard-config data):

| Console keymap (enrollment) | Helper writes | Mismatch at the prompt |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cz`: Arch renames `qwertz/cz.map` to `cz-qwertz`, so `cz` is QWERTY | `cz` (QWERTZ, two-letter fallback) | Y and Z swapped; some shifted number-row keys also differ |
| `no-latin1` | `no` | Shift+4 gives `¤` instead of `$`. The key right of Å gives dead keys instead of `~` and `^`. Shift on the key right of `+` gives dead grave instead of `` ` `` |
| `de_CH-latin1` | `ch(de_nodeadkeys)` | The console's dead `^`, `` ` ``, `~`, `¨` and `´` become literal characters |

```text
existing install, KEYMAP=cz only
  before: Plymouth reads keys through console cz (QWERTY)     -> same keymap as enrollment
  after:  migration writes XKBLAYOUT=cz and rebuilds
          Plymouth uses XKB cz (QWERTZ)                        -> Y/Z typed differently
```

**Impact:** after this migration, a passphrase containing an affected character no longer matches as typed at the LUKS prompt for these users. Not boot-tested.

**Suggested change:** only write XKB coordinates checked key by key against the console keymap. `cz` with variant `qwerty` fixes Y/Z for Arch's `cz`, and plain `ch` keeps the dead keys of `de_CH-latin1`, but neither is an exact match, and `no-latin1` has no exact XKB equivalent. Alternatively, leave KEYMAP-only files to Plymouth's console-keymap path and fix the desktop layout separately. Open PRs #11056, #11418 and #8685 change the same keymap inputs.

### `XKBLAYOUT=ua` with Arch's plymouth 26.134.222-3

Arch's plymouth packaging commit `159d7694` (26.134.222-3, 2026-09-24) makes the plymouth initcpio hook add `/etc/vconsole.conf` whenever it is non-empty. Omarchy's drop-in can only append to `FILES`, so from that build on its non-Latin exclusion no longer keeps a file out of the initramfs.

The PR's two-letter fallback writes `XKBLAYOUT=ua` for `KEYMAP=ua`, which has no `kbd-model-map` row. It does this during install, in `apply_keyboard` and in the migration.

| `KEYMAP=ua` install | plymouth -2 | plymouth -3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without the PR (KEYMAP only) | Bundled; console `ua` keymap, Latin by default | Same |
| With the PR (`XKBLAYOUT=ua`) | Excluded by drop-in; US prompt | Bundled; XKB `ua`, Cyrillic letter keys |

**Impact:** with plymouth -3, a Latin passphrase enrolled on the console becomes untypeable for `ua` users, the lockout the drop-in's exclusion was meant to prevent. Which plymouth build Omarchy's stable and edge channels currently serve was not checked.

**Suggested change:** do not derive `XKBLAYOUT` from the two-letter fallback for non-Latin keymaps, at minimum `ua`. Separately, the same packaging change bypasses the exclusion for base installs whose firstboot-written `XKBLAYOUT` is non-Latin (for example `il`), which the PR's comments rely on. That may warrant its own issue.

### A failed rebuild is marked complete on retry

The migration decides to rebuild from `OMARCHY_VCONSOLE_XKB_CHANGED`, which only records whether the current run wrote the file.

```text
run 1: write XKBLAYOUT=fr -> sudo limine-mkinitcpio fails -> exit 1, no marker
run 2: XKBLAYOUT already set -> CHANGED=0 -> exit 0 -> marker written, no rebuild
```

The real `bin/omarchy-migrate` ran twice with a rebuild stub that failed once, and the result matched the sketch. Run 2 marked the migration complete with no successful rebuild.

**Impact:** a transient rebuild failure, for example a Limine or mkinitcpio error, leaves the old initramfs in place until some unrelated rebuild such as a kernel update, with no retry and no message.

**Suggested change:** keep the need to rebuild across runs, for example by recording a pending-rebuild flag that is cleared only after a successful rebuild, or by rebuilding for any Latin layout whenever the migration runs (one extra rebuild on installs that were already complete).

**Optional (`set -u` safety):** the new `${XKBVARIANT%%,*}` in `omarchy_hooks.conf` is not `set -u` safe. `test/shell.d/nvidia-kms-hook-test.sh` still passes but prints `XKBVARIANT: unbound variable` when the sourced `vconsole.conf` has no `XKBVARIANT`. Reading it as `${XKBVARIANT:-}` into a variable before stripping `%%,*` avoids this. mkinitcpio itself does not use `-u`.

**Verified:** `luks-keyboard-layout-test.sh` (12/12), `hyprland-keyboard-layout-test.sh` (7/7) and `nvidia-kms-hook-test.sh` (9/9) pass at `c37fb5eb`, and `bash -n` is clean on the changed shell files.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source comparison of `e97fe6d2` and `c37fb5eb`. Isolated tests used private config files and recorded stubs for `sudo` and the Limine rebuild, and ran the real migration runner for the retry case. Keymaps were compared with kbd and xkeyboard-config data. The Plymouth, mkinitcpio, systemd and Arch packaging behaviour described comes from their source. No system was booted, and no real Plymouth prompt, encrypted install, sudo or UKI build was tested. The Plymouth build on Omarchy's package channels was not checked.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
